I farm the way I know best: I keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the safest way for me to get grain from the same field twice in one year, and I leave a smaller piece for cotton because I have grown it a long time and I know how to handle it. I am 64, my family labor is limited, and I have well irrigation, so I will not make the plan too complicated. I will put 6.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and 2.5 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give it moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few times, and use rotary tillage because it is easier for me and fits my usual practice. After wheat harvest, I will sow maize on that same 6.0 mu with hybrid seed, give it a bit more nitrogen, irrigate in the key stages, and keep field work simple. For cotton, I will stay cautious, use improved seed, fertilize steadily, irrigate a few times through the season, and spray more often than grain because insects are usually the bigger problem there. I am choosing this plan because it matches my age, my experience, my water access, and the need to keep income and food production steady without taking extra risk.
